items.title: Section: When Not to Give a Body Part, Even to a Genuine Request — Priority, Malice, and a Deranged Mind

items.zh: 彼菩薩為令意樂得清淨故，須捨現前利眾生事，而施身分。由彼意樂已清淨故，不應棄捨正現在前利眾生事，而施身分。
items.en: If a bodhisattva's giving-intention is not yet pure, in order to purify it, they should set aside the task of benefiting beings currently at hand and give the body part instead. But if their giving-intention is already pure, they should not abandon the vast task of benefiting beings currently at hand in order to give the body part.

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，若魔眾天懷惱亂心，現前來乞身分支節，不應分碎支節施與。何以故？勿彼當獲上品過罪及損害故。
items.en: If malicious heavenly demons, harbouring intent to provoke destruction, come seeking a body part, bodhisattvas should not sever it and give it to them. ... This is so that they do not incur the gravest fault and harm upon themselves.

items.zh: 如魔眾天，如是於彼所使眾生，當知亦爾。
或有眾生癡狂心亂，來求菩薩身分支節，亦不應碎支節施與。何以故？由彼不住自性心故，不為義利而求乞故，其心狂亂不自在故，空有種種浮妄言說，是故不應施彼身分。
items.en: If a being, confused and deranged in mind, comes seeking a body part, bodhisattvas likewise should not sever it and give it to them. Because that being does not abide in their own genuine mind, does not ask out of any genuine purpose, and their mind, deranged and out of control, produces only empty, groundless speech, a body part should not be given to them.

items.title: When Giving a Body Part Is Right, and the Principle for Internal Giving Closes

items.zh: 除上所說，與上相違，來求菩薩身支節者，隨其所欲應施彼身，隨所欲為，繫屬於彼、隨順於彼，或分支節而施與之。當知是名菩薩於內所可施物，或應施與、或不應與。
items.en: Apart from what has been described, in cases contrary to those, when someone comes seeking a bodhisattva's body or a part of it, the body should be given exactly as they wish, to do with as they will, belonging to them, following their will, or a specific part severed and given to them. This should be understood as a bodhisattva's principle regarding what may or may not be given from what is given from within.

items.title: Section: Nine Kinds of External Objects — Poison and Weapons Given Only to Heal, Never to Harm

items.zh: 又諸菩薩於外施物，若有眾生來求毒、火、刀、酒等物，或為自害、或為害他，即不應施。若有眾生來求毒、火、刀、酒等物，或自饒益、或饒益他，是即應施。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, regarding external objects to give: if a being seeks poison, fire, a blade, or alcohol in order to harm themselves or another, this should not be given. If a being seeks poison, fire, a blade, or alcohol in order to benefit themselves or another, this should be given.

items.title: Never Giving What Isn't Genuinely One's Own to Give

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，不以屬他非同意物而行惠施。又諸菩薩，不行媒媾，以他妻妾而行布施。又諸菩薩，不以有虫飲食等物而行惠施。
items.en: Bodhisattvas do not give away an object belonging to someone else without their consent. Bodhisattvas do not act as a go-between, giving access to another's wife or consort. Bodhisattvas do not give food or drink known to contain living creatures.

items.title: Section: Frivolous Gifts — Never Feeding Corruption, But Given Freely When They Build Genuine Trust

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，若有眾生來求種種能引戲樂、能引無義所施之物，不應施與。何以故？若施彼時，雖暫令彼於菩薩所心生歡喜，而復令彼廣作種種不饒益事。謂因施故，令彼多行憍逸惡行，身壞已後墮諸惡趣。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, if a being comes seeking various objects meant purely for amusement, carrying no genuine benefit, do not give them. Why is this? Because giving them, though it might briefly bring that being joy towards the bodhisattva, would go on to cause them to do a great many harmful things — since, because of the gift, that being comes to indulge heavily in arrogant, heedless misconduct, and after the body perishes, falls into the miserable realms.

items.zh: 若有種種戲樂等具雖復施與，不令眾生墮諸惡趣，亦不增長諸不善根，菩薩為欲令彼眾生，因此所施戲樂等具，攝受饒益，心生淨信，易可化導、易可成熟，隨彼所求悉皆施與。
items.en: If various objects meant for amusement, though given, would not cause a being to fall into the miserable realms nor strengthen any unwholesome root, and giving them would draw that being towards genuine benefit, give rise to pure faith, and make them easier to guide and ripen, bodhisattvas give exactly what is asked.

items.title: Section: Never Teaching the Skills of Harm, Never Aiding Blood Sacrifice

items.zh: 是諸菩薩若有來求諸戲樂事，何者應施？何者不施？謂諸菩薩終不施人捕獵等法。
items.en: If beings come seeking entertainment-related activities, which should be given and which not? Bodhisattvas never teach anyone the techniques of hunting or trapping.

items.zh: 又於雜穢諸祠祀中，作大方便多集眾生，損害其命，獲無量罪。於彼祠祀終不自作，亦不教他，亦不於彼諸天寺中殺羊祠祀。
items.en: And regarding impure sacrificial rites that gather great numbers of beings through elaborate means only to take their lives, incurring immeasurable fault, bodhisattvas never perform such rites themselves, never teach them to others, and never kill sheep in sacrificial rites even within temples to the gods.

items.title: Section: Never Providing the Grounds or Tools for Harming Life, Never Assisting Revenge

items.zh: 若有來求或水、或陸無量眾生所依止處，為欲殺害彼生命故，菩薩知已，終不施與。若有來求罩羅、罝、弶，為害眾生及為習學，皆不施與。
items.en: If someone comes seeking a place on water or land that countless beings depend on, intending to kill them there, bodhisattvas, once they know this, never give it. If someone comes seeking nets or snares or traps, whether to harm beings or merely to learn how, none of it is given.

items.zh: 若有怨家來求酬隙，為欲呵罵、縛錄、殺害、奪財、治罰，終不施與。
items.en: If an enemy comes seeking out an old grievance, wishing to curse, bind, kill, rob, or punish someone under a bodhisattva's protection, that person is never handed over.

items.title: Section: The Rule in Brief, and When Luxury or Entertainment Should Be Given Freely

items.zh: 以要言之，所有一切逼迫、損害他諸有情戲樂等具，有來求者，是諸菩薩皆不施與。
items.en: Stated concisely: whatever entertainment-related object or activity would oppress or harm other beings, whoever requests it, bodhisattvas never give.

items.zh: 若復種種象馬車輿、衣服莊嚴、珍妙飲食、習歌舞等，及諸樂器、塗飾香鬘、珍玩眾具、園林樓觀、舍宅侍女、習學種種工巧業處。如是一切戲樂等具，為欲令其於菩薩所因此發起清淨信心，有來求者悉皆施與。
items.en: But various fine carriages, clothing and adornments, exquisite food, song and dance, musical instruments, perfumes and garlands, precious objects, gardens and mansions, homes and attendants, or training in various genuine crafts — all such things, when giving them will draw the recipient towards pure faith in the bodhisattva, are given freely to whoever requests them.

items.title: Food Withheld From the Sick and the Gluttonous, and Never Aiding Self-Harm

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，若有病者來求非量、非宜飲食，亦不施與。若有眾生食飽滿已，性多饞嗜，數復來求珍妙飲食，亦不施與。
items.en: If someone ill comes seeking food in an improper amount or of an unsuitable kind, this is not given. If a being, already full, is by nature given to gluttony and repeatedly seeks exquisite food, this too is not given.

items.zh: 若諸眾生愁憂所逼，求欲殺害歐擊自身，食毒、墜巖、投淵、赴火，皆悉不應施其所欲。
items.en: If a being, overwhelmed by despair, seeks to kill or beat themselves, ingest poison, leap from a cliff, drown, or set themselves ablaze, none of this desire should ever be granted.

items.title: Section: Parents and Teachers Are Never Given Away — A Debt That Outlasts Even Their Own Cruelty

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，若有來求父母師長，定不應施。何以故？以諸菩薩於其父母尊重師長乳哺養育微有恩者，於長夜中常思頂戴不生厭倦，恒持自身繫屬隨順，任所屠害、捶縛、貨賣。尚自不敢竊懷施心，何況顯然施來求者。
items.en: If someone comes seeking a bodhisattva's own parents or teachers, this is absolutely never given. Why is this? Because bodhisattvas, towards parents, honoured teachers, those who nursed and raised them, and anyone who has shown them even the smallest kindness, constantly reflect through the long night of life on carrying that debt with reverence, never growing weary, keeping themselves devoted and compliant to them — even should those parents or teachers wish to slaughter, beat, bind, or sell the bodhisattva outright, the bodhisattva would not dare even privately consider giving them away in return, let alone openly give them to someone else who asks.

blocks.text: A long list of what a bodhisattva will not give, whoever asks. It reads like a set of ethical boundaries for generosity.

If one's intention to give is not yet pure, one should give a body part to purify it, even setting aside other work. But not to "malicious demons wishing to provoke destruction", nor to someone "confused and deranged in mind", who does not truly want it. Master Cháng Bǎi comments on the first case.

"If a being seeks poison, fire, a blade, or alcohol to harm themselves or another, it is not given." If they seek it to heal or to benefit, it may be. Master Cháng Bǎi: used properly, even poison heals, like morphine for pain.

"Bodhisattvas do not give away another's property without consent", nor act as a go-between to another's spouse, nor give food crawling with insects. Venerable Miào Jìng: giving insect-eaten things is not done.

Objects of amusement that would lead a being towards the lower realms are not given; those that harm no one and "draw that being towards genuine benefit" may be. Venerable Miào Jìng: once they have faith, they are "easy to guide".

"Bodhisattvas never teach hunting or trapping", nor perform or assist sacrifices that kill. They never give a place, nets, or snares for killing. They never hand over someone under their protection to an enemy seeking revenge.
"Whatever would oppress or harm other beings, whoever requests it, bodhisattvas never give." But fine vehicles, clothes, music, perfumes, gardens, homes may be given freely when they harm no one.

Food unsuitable for an illness, or more for a glutton, is not given. Help for self-harm "should never be granted". And "if someone asks for a bodhisattva's own parents or teachers, they are absolutely never given".

quiz.q: "In order to purify it, they should set aside the task of benefiting beings currently at hand and give the body part." The English adds "If a bodhisattva's giving-intention is not yet pure." Does Master Cháng Bǎi's explanation support this?
options: yes: when intention is not yet pure and one is reluctant, one should all the more give; when already pure, one should not abandon the work, or many would lose their support
give the body in both cases
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: when the bodhisattva's intention is not yet pure and they cannot bear to give, all the more should they give — giving what is hard to give purifies the mind. When already pure, they should not, because many people would lose their support and their chance to plant wholesome roots. The English addition agrees with the lecture.

quiz.q: When a being seeks poison, fire, a blade, or alcohol, in what case should the bodhisattva give it?
quiz.why: "If a being seeks poison, fire, a blade, or alcohol in order to harm themselves or another, this should not be given. If … in order to benefit themselves or another, this should be given."

quiz.q: What example does Master Cháng Bǎi give of a request for poison that should be granted?
options: long-acting morphine for a terminal cancer patient, or snake venom made into antivenom
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: seeking poison is not always bad — used properly it can heal, as with long-acting morphine for a terminal cancer patient, or snake venom made into antivenom.

quiz.q: "Bodhisattvas do not give food or drink containing creatures." How do the two lectures differ?
options: Miào Jìng: things insects have already eaten; Cháng Bǎi: things with insects in them, so eating them kills and both parties break precepts
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: giving things that insects have eaten — bodhisattvas do not do this. Master Cháng Bǎi: things with insects in them, because eating them kills, so both giver and receiver break the precepts. The English "known to contain living creatures" follows Master Cháng Bǎi's reading.

quiz.q: When people seek entertainment-related activities, what does the treatise say bodhisattvas never give anyone?
options: the techniques of hunting and trapping
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas never teach anyone the techniques of hunting or trapping." Venerable Miào Jìng: bodhisattvas will never give anyone the method of netting birds and beasts.

quiz.q: "Nets, snares, or traps, whether to harm beings or merely to learn how — none is given." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "to learn how"?
options: not going out to shoot birds or catch fish now, but wanting to learn how to use these things
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "I'm not going to shoot birds or catch fish now, but I want to learn how to use these things." He also explains that a "zhào" is for catching fish and a "luó" is a net for catching birds.

quiz.q: If someone comes seeking a bodhisattva's own parents or teachers, what does the treatise say?
options: give if the person is sincere
never to be given; bodhisattvas dare not even secretly entertain the thought, let alone openly give them
quiz.why: "If someone comes seeking a bodhisattva's own parents or teachers, this is absolutely never given." Bodhisattvas do not dare even secretly harbour the thought of giving them, let alone openly. Venerable Miào Jìng: though bodhisattvas train in the perfection of giving, they do not give away parents or teachers.
